draft.title: Pure substances and mixtures
card: It has only one kind of particle. Distilled water is pure, because every particle in it is a water particle.
It has two or more substances mixed together but not joined. Each substance keeps its own properties.
Because the substances in a mixture are not joined, they can be separated by physical means. Examples are sieving, picking out pieces or filtering.
A pure substance cannot be split into other substances by physical means. Air, sea water and soil are mixtures.
draft.remember: Pure: one kind of particle. Mixture: two or more, and a physical method can separate them.

a.q: Which of these is a pure substance?
a.why: Distilled water has only one kind of particle, so it is pure. Sea water has salt mixed in with the water, so it is a mixture even though it looks clear.
a.clue: Look for the one with only one kind of particle.

b.q: Liam stirs sand and iron filings together in a dish. He then pulls the iron out with a magnet. What does this show about the sand and iron?
opts: A mixture formed, so a physical method can separate it
A pure substance formed, so a magnet can separate it
They were joined, so the magnet broke them apart
A mixture formed, so only a chemical change can split it
b.why: The sand and iron were only mixed, not joined, so a magnet could pull them apart. This is a physical method. Stirring did not make a pure substance, because two kinds of particle were still present.
b.clue: Did stirring join the two substances or only mix them?

b.best: A mixture formed, so a physical method can separate it
